name: program-far-serve-at
in:
# Far copy, step 25.4 (7.2.42, 7.2.45): the answerer of far_serve.tw for any position of a window of 1024 cells. A text of language 4: the same protocol over its
# stdin/stdout (the shell connects the stdout of the asker to this stdin and this stdout to the stdin of the asker); the reads and the writes of a cell by its number are
# the computed address of `copy`, `&win@&idx`: not `lut` and `store` but a copy by the value of the cell idx (the pass l4c makes of it the same words of language 3).
# The record of a request: fixed size, 6 bytes, read by three `key`:   op (8 bits)   pos (32 bits)   dat (8 bits)
#   op = 0 (all 8 bits)  stop (no answer)      op = 1  get: answer one byte, win[pos]      op = 2  put: win[pos] = dat (no answer)
#   any other op (3, 4, 16, 255 ...) is a spoiled record: it is skipped, nothing is answered, the next record is read (only op = 0 whole stops the answerer).
#   a number is stored as `key` stores it: the first bit of the stream is the lowest bit (pos: 4 bytes, the lowest byte first).
#   pos is the number of a byte; out of the window (pos >= 1024): get answers a byte of ones (255) = the prohibitive price; put changes nothing.
#   The end of the stdin (the channel is closed) is a stop: op is zeroed before every read and a read at EOF leaves it as it was.
# The window is the array win: 2^10 cells of 8 bits, the largest array of language 3 (K up to 10); the first 8 cells are COPYMACH as in far_serve.tw, the rest are zeros.
# lt works over 8 nibbles (c3 is 9 bits, the test is c3[8]); the index is the 10 low bits of pos (pos[0:10], the width K of the array).
:op data 8 0
:pos data 32 0
:dat data 8 0
:ans data 8 0
:zero8 data 8 0
:one8 data 8 1
:two8 data 8 2
:e data 2 0
:ones data 8 255
:lim data 32 1024
:c3 data 9 0
:win array 10 8
:init data 64 "COPYMACH"
:i0 data 10 0
:i1 data 10 1
:i2 data 10 2
:i3 data 10 3
:i4 data 10 4
:i5 data 10 5
:i6 data 10 6
:i7 data 10 7
:main block
copy &win@&i0 &init[0:8]
copy &win@&i1 &init[8:16]
copy &win@&i2 &init[16:24]
copy &win@&i3 &init[24:32]
copy &win@&i4 &init[32:40]
copy &win@&i5 &init[40:48]
copy &win@&i6 &init[48:56]
copy &win@&i7 &init[56:64]
goto &loop
:loop block
copy &op &zero8
key &op
key &pos
key &dat
lt &pos &lim &c3
eq &op &zero8 &e
if &e[1] &done &isget
:isget block
eq &op &one8 &e
if &e[1] &get &notget
:get block
if &c3[8] &getin &getout
:getin block
copy &ans &win@&pos[0:10]
emit &ans
goto &loop
:getout block
emit &ones
goto &loop
:notget block
eq &op &two8 &e
if &e[1] &put &loop
:put block
if &c3[8] &putin &loop
:putin block
copy &win@&pos[0:10] &dat
goto &loop
:done block
halt

# the top 32 bits, 0 = the neighbour by stdin and stdout; the position in the low 96 bits: here the bit of the byte, a multiple of 8). The pass l4c makes of
# `copy &x <far>` the requests get (one byte each, the answer is read into &x) and of `copy <far> &x` the requests put. The protocol is that of far_serve.tw
# (op 8 bits, pos 32 bits = the number of the byte, dat 8 bits). The stdout of this program is the stdin of far_serve.tw and its stdin is the stdout of far_serve.tw;
# the cells are written to stderr (warn) at the end. A cell starts as zeros: the answer outside the window is ones, no answer at all (the channel is closed) leaves zeros.
# The window of the answerer is COPYMACH (8 bytes). The copies, the byte numbers in the window and what must be read:
#   w8   <- bytes 0..7                       COPYMACH
#   x4   <- bytes 2..5                       PYMA
#   bytes 5, 6 <- "OK" (put)
#   y2   <- bytes 5, 6                       OK
#   x4b  <- bytes 4..7                       MOKH
#   o1   <- byte 8 (outside)                 255
#   t4   <- bytes 6..9 (7 is the last cell)  K H 255 255
#   bytes 8, 9 <- "OK" (put outside: nothing changes)
#   hi4  <- byte 2^28 + 3 (outside; the low bits are the cell 3, the 32-bit number must not be cut)   255 x 4
#   byte 2^28 + 3 <- "O" (put outside: the cell 3 stays)
#   y1   <- byte 3                           Y
:w8 data 64 0
:x4 data 32 0
:ok data 16 "OK"
:y2 data 16 0
:x4b data 32 0
:o1 data 8 0
:t4 data 32 0
:hi4 data 32 0
:oo data 8 "O"
:y1 data 8 0
:stop data 48 0
:main block
copy &w8 0x200000000000000000000000000000000
copy &x4 0x200000000000000000000000000000010
copy 0x200000000000000000000000000000028 &ok
copy &y2 0x200000000000000000000000000000028
copy &x4b 0x200000000000000000000000000000020
copy &o1 0x200000000000000000000000000000040
copy &t4 0x200000000000000000000000000000030
copy 0x200000000000000000000000000000040 &ok
copy &hi4 0x200000000000000000000000080000018
copy 0x200000000000000000000000080000018 &oo
copy &y1 0x200000000000000000000000000000018
goto &fin
# the stop (op = 0, a whole record), then the cells to stderr
:fin block
emit &stop
goto &show
:show block
warn &w8
warn &x4
warn &y2
warn &x4b
warn &o1
warn &t4
warn &hi4
warn &y1
halt
